title: Bruins to retire Patrice Bergeron’s No. 37 in recognition of ‘remarkable’ career
content:
The Boston Bruins will retire Patrice Bergeron’s No. 37 next season, the team announced Thursday. It will be the 14th number to hang in the TD Garden rafters. Zdeno Chara’s No. 33 was retired Jan. 15.

“Across his remarkable 20-year career, Patrice Bergeron established himself as one of the greatest two-way forwards the game has seen and as a cornerstone to one of the most successful periods of Bruins hockey in our franchise’s history,” team president Cam Neely said in a statement.

Bergeron, who retired in July 2023, was selected in the second round in the 2003 draft. He played all 1,294 games in the NHL with the Bruins. His stat line was impressive, notching 427 goals and 1,040 points, the third most in team history behind Ray Bourque and Johnny Bucyk. Additionally, Bergeron added 50 goals and 128 points over 170 career playoff games while usually being tasked with keeping the other team’s best offensive players in check. The 2011 Stanley Cup champion won Olympic gold with Team Canada in 2010 and 2014.

Bergeron won the Selke Trophy six times, an NHL record, as the league’s best two-way forward. While maintaining his defensive presence, Bergeron transitioned later in his career into an offensive threat and power-play specialist in the bumper position. He centered the Bruins’ top line between Brad Marchand and David Pastrnak and was used by his coaches in all situations.

It is widely believed that the native of L’Ancienne-Lorette, Que., will become a first-ballot Hall of Famer when the 2026 inductees are announced Monday.

The 40-year-old still lives in the greater Boston area. Upon the suggestion of coach Marco Sturm, his former linemate, Bergeron has counseled several current Bruins, including Morgan Geekie and Fraser Minten, during occasional sessions at Warrior Ice Arena.
